newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close week on firm note.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close week on firm note.

text.p: Argentine stocks extended their upward bounce at the close Friday and were seen holding steady, dealers said.
"The market is likely to stay firm and should be aided by a technical rebound on Wall Street next week, although buyers will remain cautious," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV rose 1.0 percent to a two-week high of 730.41 and ended up 2.6 percent in the week.
Analysts said the bolsa had already discounted a rise in the U.S. Federal Funds rate to 5.5 percent from 5.25 percent when the Federal Reserve meets Tuesday.
"The likely rate hike has been digested and partially offset by expectations of a sovereign debt upgrade by Standard & Poor's," said Bonanno.
S&P is expected to either confirm its current BB- rating or announce an upgrade early next month.
"We'll probably see more buying ahead of the S&P announcement, because economic fundamentals remain very strong and there's reason to think we're on the brink of an upgrade," another trader said.
The bolsa's all-share index closed up 0.7 percent, with risers pounding decliners 50 to 10 and 13 stocks closing flat.
Floor volume picked up to 25.7 million pesos from 20 million Thursday, while over-the-counter deals swelled to a hefty tally of 180.2 million pesos from an already strong 158.2 million Thursday.
Best main-tier performers were foods giant Molinos, which jumped 3.1 percent, and electricity distributor Central Costanera and steelmaker Siderar, both up 2.9 percent.
The only MerVal loser was pulp and paper maker Celulosa, down 4.5 percent.
